title: Physics-informed machine learning guides experimental Curie-temperature validation in Ce–Zr–Fe alloys
summary: A machine-learning model trained on measured Curie temperatures selected two compositions in the (Zr1−xCex)Fe2 system, (Zr0.16Ce0.84)Fe2 and (Zr0.94Ce0.06)Fe2, for experimental validation. The study also reports a relationship between electronic states near the Fermi level and Curie temperature, including a breakdown of de Gennes scaling below a rare-earth-content threshold. This is a materials discovery study, not evidence of a finished permanent magnet or deployed technology.
ai_technology: Physics-informed machine-learning model trained on experimentally measured Curie temperatures
organization: Ames National Laboratory, U.S. Department of Energy; Iowa State University

evidence.tested: The authors selected (Zr0.16Ce0.84)Fe2 and (Zr0.94Ce0.06)Fe2 for experimental Curie-temperature validation of the model-guided predictions.
evidence.unknown: The exact Curie-temperature measurements and uncertainty are not included here. This study does not establish a finished permanent magnet, device-level performance, or zero-carbon deployment.
evidence.ai_role: A learned model trained on experimentally measured Curie temperatures was used to predict multicomponent magnetic-material properties and select the two Ce–Zr–Fe compositions for experimental validation. The paper also reports that the model captured electronic-structure trends associated with Curie temperature.

source_review.scope: Primary ACS publisher abstract, article metadata and supporting-information description. Full article numerical Curie-temperature results and uncertainty were not reviewed.
